editorial.intro: A parametric garment system built around body form, measurements and adjustable design parameters.
editorial.introFa: یک سیستم پارامتریک طراحی پوشاک بر پایه‌ی فرم بدن، اندازه‌ها و پارامترهای قابل تنظیم.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: Exploring how a garment can respond to the body
caseStudy.body: Veblen is an independent exploration of a parametric garment system, connecting body form, measurements and adjustable design parameters in a digital environment.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: Make the relationship between body, input and outcome legible
caseStudy.body: The central design question was how to help someone understand the connection between a body model, its measurements and the garment form those inputs can influence—without exposing the system as a set of disconnected technical controls.

caseStudy.label: 03 / EXPERIENCE MODEL
caseStudy.title: Organise the experience around a clear sequence
caseStudy.body: I framed the concept around three connected parts: visualising the body, mapping measurements and exploring garment variations. This gives the interaction a comprehensible structure from input to visual outcome.

caseStudy.label: 04 / INTERACTION & VISUALISATION
caseStudy.title: Make abstract parameters easier to read
caseStudy.body: The design exploration uses 3D body visualisation and measurement mapping to give the parametric system a more tangible interface. Garment exploration is presented as a visual process rather than an isolated set of values.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A connected model for parametric exploration
caseStudy.body: The concept brings body representation, measurement inputs and garment variation into one product direction. Its value is the clarity of the proposed interaction model—not a claim of production deployment or measured user impact.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: Independent product design exploration
caseStudy.body: Concept direction and product-interface exploration across the parametric garment system. Independent project, 2025–2026.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: The structure behind the exploration
impact.note: Counts describe the documented design scope and portfolio evidence—not production usage or business performance.

metrics.detail: Body visualisation as the spatial reference

impact.foot: The impact is expressed through a coherent model for exploring form and fit. No adoption, accuracy or conversion uplift is claimed.

editorial.intro: An employee experience platform connecting survey creation, feedback and people analytics.
editorial.introFa: پلتفرم تجربه‌ی کارکنان برای ساخت نظرسنجی، دریافت بازخورد و تحلیل داده‌های منابع انسانی.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: From employee feedback to actionable understanding
caseStudy.body: Pulse Check is an employee experience platform connecting survey creation, employee feedback and people analytics for HR teams.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: Keep the feedback loop understandable end to end
caseStudy.body: The experience spans survey setup, active participation and the interpretation of results. The design challenge was to make these stages feel connected, so collecting feedback and understanding it are parts of one workflow.

caseStudy.label: 03 / WORKFLOW DESIGN
caseStudy.title: Structure the journey from collection to interpretation
caseStudy.body: I worked across survey setup, active survey states, reporting, heatmaps and open comments. The design narrative follows the information as it moves from a survey into quantitative patterns and qualitative feedback.

caseStudy.label: 04 / INFORMATION HIERARCHY
caseStudy.title: Let summary and detail support each other
caseStudy.body: The reporting experience brings visual patterns and written comments into the same broader context. Heatmaps help surface response patterns, while open comments preserve the detail behind those patterns.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A more connected feedback and reporting experience
caseStudy.body: The designed surfaces connect survey operations with reporting and employee comments, helping HR teams move between an overview of responses and the feedback that adds context. This is a design outcome, not a measured engagement or decision-making uplift.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: Product Designer · primary design ownership
caseStudy.body: I led the product design work within a two-person design team. The second designer’s involvement was primarily feedback and critique. Project shown within the Jobvision employment period, 2023–2025.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: A feedback loop, represented in one system
impact.note: Scope indicators are based on the supplied project screens and confirmed team structure; they are not product-performance metrics.
impact.foot: The design contribution connects survey operations with quantitative reporting and qualitative feedback. No survey completion, engagement or retention uplift is inferred.

editorial.intro: A map-led guide to discovering places, routes and local experiences across Iran.
editorial.introFa: راهنمایی نقشه‌محور برای کشف مکان‌ها، مسیرها و تجربه‌های محلی در ایران.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: A cultural atlas built around discovery
caseStudy.body: Iran Unseen is an independent, map-led digital experience for discovering places, routes and local experiences across Iran.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: A map needs context to become useful
caseStudy.body: A map can show where something is, but discovery also depends on understanding what a place offers and how it relates to other places. The design challenge was to connect geographic orientation with the information needed to choose a next step.

caseStudy.label: 03 / DISCOVERY MODEL
caseStudy.title: Make the map the organising layer
caseStudy.body: I framed the experience around map-based discovery, supported by place cards and categories. This keeps geographic context present while people browse individual destinations.

caseStudy.label: 04 / JOURNEY & SUPPORTING ELEMENTS
caseStudy.title: Connect places, routes and saved locations
caseStudy.body: The concept brings routes and saved places into the discovery model, extending the experience beyond a single point on a map and giving exploration a structure that can continue.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A connected framework for local exploration
caseStudy.body: The design establishes a map-led model that links places, categories, routes and saved locations. It presents geographic discovery and place information as parts of one experience, without claiming validated travel outcomes.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: Independent Product Designer
caseStudy.body: Independent product and experience design exploration. The project is listed under 2025–2026 as a provisional period; exact project dates remain unconfirmed.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: Four building blocks for discovery
impact.note: These numbers describe the concept structure and the supplied portfolio material—not usage, destination coverage or travel outcomes.
impact.foot: The design impact is the proposed connection between geographic context and place information. No visitor, booking or engagement metrics are claimed.

passport.periodBasis: Associated with Jobvision; exact project dates are not separately stated.

editorial.intro: A recruitment workspace for managing applicant information and hiring workflows.
editorial.introFa: فضای کاری جذب نیرو برای مدیریت اطلاعات متقاضیان و فرایندهای استخدام.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: A focused view into recruitment operations
caseStudy.body: Jobvision’s Applicant Tracking System supports recruitment operations. This case study deliberately focuses on the dashboard experience and its mobile presentation.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: Make a dense overview easier to scan
caseStudy.body: Recruitment dashboards bring jobs, applicants and changing statuses into one operational space. The design challenge addressed here was how to establish visual priority across the overview without losing the context of the information.

caseStudy.label: 03 / INFORMATION HIERARCHY
caseStudy.title: Separate the overview from supporting detail
caseStudy.body: The dashboard design focuses on grouping related information and creating a clear distinction between summary content and supporting detail. The aim is to make the overall workspace easier to read at a glance.

caseStudy.label: 04 / RESPONSIVE ADAPTATION
caseStudy.title: Carry the dashboard logic into a mobile view
caseStudy.body: I adapted the dashboard presentation for a narrower mobile viewport, considering how the information hierarchy and interface composition translate beyond the desktop layout.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A dashboard-first design contribution
caseStudy.body: The work represented in this case is the ATS dashboard and its mobile view. The outcome is a focused overview experience; it should not be read as ownership of the wider ATS product or its other workflows.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: Product Designer · dashboard experience
caseStudy.body: My contribution focused on the ATS dashboard and its mobile presentation. Other ATS screens and workflows were outside my design scope. Project shown within the Jobvision employment period, 2023–2025.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: A deliberately focused design scope
impact.note: Counts describe the supplied design deliverables and presentation contexts—not the full ATS product.
impact.foot: The impact is the clearer hierarchy and mobile adaptation within the dashboard scope. No claim is made about the complete ATS workflow or hiring-performance metrics.

editorial.intro: An AI creative workspace presented across desktop, Persian-language and mobile interfaces.
editorial.introFa: فضای خلاقیت مبتنی بر هوش مصنوعی در نسخه‌های دسکتاپ، فارسی و موبایل.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: One workspace. Multiple creative capabilities.
caseStudy.body: Humaani is an AI creative workspace bringing creative tools and related workflows into one product environment. The design task was to make that breadth feel like a coherent workspace.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: The challenge was connection, not just individual screens.
caseStudy.body: Distinct capabilities needed a shared structure. Without clear relationships between modules, navigation and user journeys, the workspace could feel like a collection of separate tools.

caseStudy.label: 03 / EXPERIENCE ARCHITECTURE
caseStudy.title: Map the product before polishing the interface.
caseStudy.body: I worked on the information architecture, navigation hierarchy and cross-module flows, organising how the different parts of the workspace relate and how users move between them.

caseStudy.label: 04 / SYSTEM DESIGN
caseStudy.title: Create consistency that can scale across modules.
caseStudy.body: I developed a shared design system and reusable interface patterns to establish consistent visual and interaction rules across the product, rather than treating each area as a separate design problem.

caseStudy.label: 05 / EXPERIENCE ADAPTATION
caseStudy.title: One product language across two languages and screens.
caseStudy.body: The experience was designed for Persian and English, with responsive mobile layouts. The work considered language direction, hierarchy and layout adaptation as part of the product experience.

caseStudy.label: 06 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A more coherent foundation for an AI workspace.
caseStudy.body: The resulting design connects product structure, navigation, interface patterns and responsive bilingual experiences. This describes the delivered design scope—not a claim of measured business or usability uplift.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: The footprint of the design work
impact.note: Verified project-scope indicators. These are not conversion, retention or usability performance metrics.
impact.foot: Impact is expressed through the design foundation delivered: connected architecture, consistent interface patterns and a bilingual, responsive workspace—not through invented outcome statistics.

passport.periodBasis: User confirmed this project belongs to the Jobvision period; exact project dates are not separately stated.

editorial.intro: An executive talent platform with a focus on talent discovery and contact flows.
editorial.introFa: پلتفرم استعدادهای مدیریتی با تمرکز بر کشف استعداد و جریان‌های ارتباطی.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: A focused platform for executive talent
caseStudy.body: Mirana is an executive talent platform centred on discovering relevant profiles and creating a clear path to contact.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: Help people move from a profile to a next step
caseStudy.body: The experience needed to present executive talent with enough context for profile review, while making the next action—contact—easy to recognise across desktop and mobile.

caseStudy.label: 03 / DISCOVERY & PROFILE PRESENTATION
caseStudy.title: Keep talent information connected to the decision
caseStudy.body: The design contribution represented here focuses on the executive talent interface: presenting profile information as the central point of discovery rather than separating it from the action that follows.

caseStudy.label: 04 / CONTACT FLOW & MOBILE
caseStudy.title: Preserve the journey across touchpoints
caseStudy.body: The contact flow and mobile experience extend the profile presentation into the next step. The design focus is continuity between discovering a person, understanding the profile and initiating contact.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A direct discovery-to-contact experience
caseStudy.body: The supplied desktop and mobile screens show a connected direction across talent presentation and contact actions. This describes the designed experience, not a measured increase in contact rates or hiring outcomes.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: Product Designer · Jobvision product portfolio
caseStudy.body: Product design contribution within the Jobvision product portfolio, during the November 2023–April 2025 employment period. Exact project dates are not separately confirmed.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: From talent discovery to contact
impact.note: Scope indicators reflect the documented project material and confirmed product focus—not usage or recruitment performance.
impact.foot: The design contribution connects profile presentation with a clear contact path across web and mobile. No conversion or placement metrics are implied.

editorial.intro: An FMCG marketplace spanning store operations, shopper data and reporting.
editorial.introFa: بازارگاه کالاهای تندمصرف با ابزارهای مدیریت فروشگاه، داده‌ی خریداران و گزارش‌گیری.

caseStudy.label: 01 / PROJECT CONTEXT
caseStudy.title: A marketplace with operational and shopper-facing sides
caseStudy.body: Pinket is an FMCG marketplace spanning store operations, shopper information, product details, reporting and the shopper journey.

caseStudy.label: 02 / PROBLEM FRAMING
caseStudy.title: Bring different information needs into one product language
caseStudy.body: The product serves operational needs as well as the shopper-facing experience. Store data, shopper context, product information and reports each have different purposes; the design challenge was to keep these touchpoints coherent without flattening their differences.

caseStudy.label: 03 / INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
caseStudy.title: Give each operational area a clear role
caseStudy.body: The documented design scope covers the store dashboard, shopper overview, product information and reporting. These areas are treated as distinct operational views within the broader marketplace experience.

caseStudy.label: 04 / SHOPPER EXPERIENCE
caseStudy.title: Connect operational context with the customer journey
caseStudy.body: The shopper app journey forms the customer-facing side of the product. Bringing it into the same design narrative makes the relationship between marketplace operations and the shopper experience visible.

caseStudy.label: 05 / DESIGN OUTCOME
caseStudy.title: A broader set of connected marketplace touchpoints
caseStudy.body: The supplied designs establish a consistent interface direction across operational dashboards and the shopper journey. This describes the design scope and interface contribution, not a measured commercial uplift.

caseStudy.label: 06 / ROLE & SCOPE
caseStudy.title: UI/UX Designer · two-person design team
caseStudy.body: Product interface and experience design as part of a two-person design team at Pinket, January 2022–June 2023.

impact.label: DESIGN IMPACT / SCOPE AT A GLANCE
impact.title: Five touchpoints across the marketplace
impact.note: Counts describe the confirmed design focus and supplied portfolio visuals—not transaction volume or business performance.

metrics.detail: Store · Shopper · Product · Reports · App journey

impact.foot: The design contribution spans operational views and the shopper-facing journey. No order growth, GMV or conversion uplift is claimed.
